messages:
ryan: quick follow-up from last week's RFC review — under a mixed workload we saw starvation when the prefetch window + relaxed batching are enabled for some long-seq tenants.

sophia: can you share the repro steps and a short trace?

ryan: repro is easy on the perf rig: 40% long-seq (L=4k tokens, stream=false) + 60% short chat (L<256, streaming). with prefetch_window=8 and soft_preempt=false, short requests get delayed a lot. attached snippets below.

ryan: trace excerpt: 
```
worker-7: enqueue req T=0 tenant=alpha size=200
worker-7: prefetch started for tenant=alpha req=1234 window=8
worker-7: hold batch until window full or deadline -> long seqs dominate
worker-7: short reqs pile up -> latency spike 95% p95 ~ 800ms
```

alex: hm. sounds like two separate issues: (A) admission policy needs to account for estimated service time (not just token count), (B) prefetch should be tenant-aware to avoid monopolizing the batch pool.

cheng: Agreed. My proposal for minimal interface changes: keep the runtime <-> scheduler contract small but expressive. Add a lightweight admission hint in the request proto and an optional lease token in the response. Example sketch: 
```
// Admission hint from front-end -> scheduler
message AdmissionHint {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  int32 seq_len_est = 2;    // rough token estimate
  float priority_score = 3; // 0..1, caller hint
}

// Scheduler response
message AdmissionDecision {
  bool admitted = 1;
  int32 wait_ms_est = 2;    // best-effort
  string lease_token = 3;   // allow short-term occupancy accounting
}
```

cheng: lease_token is optional. runtime uses it to attach KV-cache ownership for the duration of the lease, so we can evict/transfer cleanly on preempt.

sophia: lease token + tenant-aware prefetch sounds good. two quick tradeoffs: (1) adding seq_len_est increases coupling to client estimator (but it's a hint so we can ignore/misuse), (2) lease tokens require a cheap coordination path — cannot be a global consensus op.

ryan: exactly. proposal: keep admission decision local to the scheduler instance (no global lock), but expose a short-lived lease token signed by the scheduler node. other nodes can validate and accept transfers. avoids sync for every admission.

alex: if we do signed tokens, we need expiry and revocation semantics. also metrics: we must emit per-tenant prefetch-time and preempt-count. otherwise debugging will be impossible.

infra-bot: deploybot: canary deployed branch "sched-lease-tokens" to perf-rig-3 (rx).

ryan: next design question — headroom calculation. the current heuristic (x% of free batch slots) is too coarse when mix includes many long sequences. cheng suggested weight-based headroom: each tenant accumulates credits proportional to historical occupancy and priority.

cheng: right. imagine credits increment = time_in_gpu_ms * priority. admission consumes credits ~ seq_len_est * model_cost_factor. low-credit tenants get admitted at lower rate. this buys fairness without strict per-tenant hard caps.

alex: sounds promising, but metrics and defaults matter. two immediate tests: (1) binary search for model_cost_factor under synthetic loads, (2) check worst-case tail for small tenants under adversarial long-seq bursts.

ryan: agree. concrete action items: 
- create prototype branch with admission hint + signed lease token (alex + ryan)
- add weight-credit accounting and default config (cheng)
- add perf tests: mixed workload with varied seq_len distribution and tenant counts (sophia)
- telemetry: emit admit_decision.{admitted,wait_ms_est,reason,lease_issued} and tenant.credit_level (infra team)

alex: I'll own the prototype infra pieces. can we target a perf run mid-next-week?

sophia: mid-next-week works if we have a simple non-cryptographic token first (HMAC) then iterate. I'll prepare the test harness.

ryan: one more UX point — keep the admission API backward compatible: if no hint provided, scheduler should fall back to current behavior. want minimal churn for Hosted API layers.

cheng: +1. also doc the semantics in a short RFC appendix: expected accuracy of seq_len_est, lease time defaults, token format.

alex: ack. I'll open a PR with the proto sketch + a README for the appendix. tagging @sophia @cheng for review.

ryan: thanks. if no objections I'll merge the prototype branch after a quick perf validate. :thumbsup:

sophia: no objections from me. excited to see if credits reduce p95 for the small-tenants.

alex: logging follow-up: include a compact sample for observability consumption: 
```
{ "ts": 1979993333, "tenant":"alpha", "admitted":false, "wait_ms_est":420, "lease":null, "seq_len_est":4100 }
```

ryan: perfect — that'll help dashboards. I'll add follow-up issue with raw graph expectations.

cheng: leaving an implementation note: avoid using seq_len_est directly for batching selection. it's an admission hint only — batching decisions should still prefer fill-rate + latency SLOs.

ryan: agreed. thanks everyone — will circle back with perf numbers and the PR links. :rocket:
